bugs.description: Author benchmark `pi` (read at line 102 from pi_codings_2ndhalf.csv, de-duplicated at line 108) is never sorted or joined by docid, but every metric (calculate_hamming_loss line 1552, F1/recall/precision via actual_list_10/actual_list_4 lines 124-128, calculate_auc line 1358, calculate_icc_scores line 1168, undergrads8/4 lines 2050-2064) compares it with the model and undergraduate matrices by row position. The model and human files are in ascending docid order; pi is not. So each article's model codes are compared with a different article's author codes.
bugs.evidence: Run outputs: identical(pi$docid, gpt4o 8 few docid) = FALSE, docid sets equal = TRUE, share of rows with the same docid at the same position = 0.0017 (outputs/targets_extracted.csv); all 18 model and 2 human data frames share one docid order (outputs/model_files_docid_order.csv). Pooled counts for GPT 4o Few Shot 8 labels, position pairing: FP 539, FN 320; docid pairing: FP 369, FN 150 (outputs/row_pairing_confusion_counts.csv). The supplement's Table A5, built in Benchmarking_Supplementary.Rmd with left_join(pi10, by = 'docid'), prints FP 369 and FN 150 (as quoted in PREREG.md). Undergraduates: position FP 401, FN 325; docid FP 256, FN 180 vs printed Table A6 FP 254, FN 180. Author-benchmark AUC is about 0.50 for every model under position pairing and about 0.75 to 0.82 under docid pairing (outputs/analysis_log_main.txt vs outputs/analysis_log_Rc.txt stargazer tables). Table A1 values match the position-paired run.

bugs.description: undergrads8 (lines 2050-2056) and undergrads4 (lines 2058-2064), labelled 'undergraduate metrics for manual addition to table', compute AUC, Recall and F1 from gpt10mat / gpt4mat (GPT 4 Turbo Zero Shot output) instead of hum10mat / hum4mat; only Hamming Loss and % 1s use the undergraduate matrices. env_fixes: none: Benchmarking_DataAnalysis.Rmd ran unmodified (working directory set by cd in scripts/run_rmd.sh; packages installed: Debian r-cran-* binaries plus irr and stargazer from CRAN into the per-run library). diffs/R_c_Benchmarking_DataAnalysis_docid_sort.diff is the pre-registered R_c analysis copy, not an environment fix.
class_reason: All six targets reproduced to the paper's rounding by running Benchmarking_DataAnalysis.Rmd exactly as deposited (batch4 class decision 4); all six conclusion criteria hold. The docid-paired rerun (R_c) changes the absolute values (T1 0.110, T2 0.093) but keeps the ranking, direction and bootstrap significance; per PROTOCOL section 7 it does not change the class.
confidence_reason: Deterministic script, unmodified, all targets matched by script with every input file checksum identical to the pre-registration download; agreement with agent B not yet known.
uncertainties: Paper values come from a browser agent's reading of the supplement in the Google Docs viewer (PREREG section 4); I did not re-open the supplement. The exact match of all six cells supports that reading.
Not a target: Table A1 prints 9.68 for Undergraduate Coders 8 '% 1s'; the script's undergrads8 '% 1s' is 9.72 (outputs/targets_extracted.csv). I did not establish why.

Row-pairing observation (bugs[0]) is confirmed by runs as a property of the deposited code and data; whether the printed Table A1 was meant to use docid pairing cannot be determined from the deposit. The paper's ranking and direction claims hold under both pairings (R_c), but the printed magnitudes (0.18, 0.15, 'by 0.03 points', AUC about 0.5) are those of the position pairing.

Under docid pairing, undergraduate FP is 256 vs 254 printed in Table A6; Table A6 comes from Benchmarking_Supplementary.Rmd (not run), which may use a different undergraduate file (AI_goldstandard_ten_v2.csv). Unverified.
Package versions differ from the author's (R 4.3.3, unpinned); here R 4.5.0 and Debian/CRAN current versions. Outputs are deterministic and matched, so drift did not matter for targets.
R_a/R_b/R_c p-values are 0 at 1000-resample resolution and are the audit's own significance reading; the paper reports no tests.
